notes:
I couldn't write these notes. My research tool turned down my very first request with a "no more tool calls remaining this turn" message, so I didn't get to read any pages. That first request was for Enduring Word's Job 31, the Ellicott, Pulpit and Gill commentaries on biblehub.com, the Precept Austin Job 31 page and the NET Bible notes.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say, give a URL for every point and never fill gaps from my own knowledge. With no pages read, I have nothing I can honestly cite. Writing verse-by-verse notes from memory and attaching URLs would break those rules, and the citations could be wrong.

When the tool is available again, please ask me to resume. I'll start with these pages, then search for the remaining traditions and other views:

1. **Traditional reading:** enduringword.com/bible-commentary/job-31/, and biblehub.com/commentaries/ followed by ellicott/job/31.htm, pulpit/job/31.htm and gill/job/31.htm. I'll also check Precept Austin's Job pages.
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:** Wesley's Notes (wesley.nnu.edu), and Reformed and Baptist pieces on Job's "covenant with my eyes" (v. 1) and his claims of integrity (vv. 6, 35–37). Those come from ligonier.org, thegospelcoalition.org, desiringgod.org and gty.org. Lutheran pieces would come from lcms.org and 1517.org.
3. **Other views:** NET Bible notes on hard verses such as v. 12 (Abaddon), v. 27 (kissing the hand toward the sun and moon) and v. 33 ("like Adam"), plus bibleodyssey.org. For Catholic and Orthodox readings, I'll look for Church Fathers on Job on newadvent.org, such as Gregory the Great's *Moralia*, and check oca.org.
